objective: Add date-based log rotation to the logservice fixture: midnight-boundary rotation to logs/app-YYYYMMDD.log, 7-file retention, and gzip compression of rotated files older than yesterday — without changing existing append behavior or breaking existing tests.
in_scope: New stateless rotation module app/rotation.py (naming, rotation decision, rotation, retention, compression; all functions take an explicit now: datetime)
Rotation trigger points in app/logger.py: LogWriter.__init__ (startup check) and LogWriter.append (date-change check before write)
New unit tests for the rotation policy (tests/test_rotation.py) and for the LogWriter wiring (tests/test_log_rotation.py)
New e2e test simulating a midnight crossing through serve() (tests/e2e/test_rotation_e2e.py)
Retention pass (7 most recent rotated files kept) and compression pass (rotated files older than yesterday gzipped) run on each rotation event

frozen_assumptions.statement: Python 3.11, stdlib only — no third-party packages may be imported.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: README platform notes; task statement says 'stdlib is fine'.

frozen_assumptions.statement: The service appends at least once per day or restarts at least daily, so an append-driven check plus a startup check covers every midnight boundary.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: README: no scheduler available, rotation must be driven from the service loop or at startup; serve() appends one line per request, and LogWriter.__init__ covers the restart case.
frozen_assumptions.invalidated_by: Product requirement that logs rotate even during multi-day zero-traffic periods without restart (would need a timer — new stage).

frozen_assumptions.statement: Every line in app.log begins with an ISO timestamp %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S written by the server loop, so the live file's date is the date of its last line.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: app/server.py serve() writes writer.append(f"{time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')} {req}") for every request.
frozen_assumptions.invalidated_by: A writer emitting timestamp-less lines (fallback defined in C1: mtime date of the live file).

frozen_assumptions.statement: At most one process appends to logs/app.log at any time.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: Fixture is a single-process service; rename-based rotation is not safe under concurrent writers, and concurrency is not in the task.
frozen_assumptions.invalidated_by: Multi-worker deployment of the fixture (would need atomic rename+lock — new stage).

frozen_assumptions.statement: A rotated file is named after the completed day — the date of the last line in the live log — not the current date.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: Task: 'each day's lines end up in logs/app-YYYYMMDD.log'; the archived lines belong to the completed day.

frozen_architecture.decision: Rotation policy (naming, decision, rotation, retention, compression) lives in a new stateless module app/rotation.py whose functions take an explicit now: datetime; LogWriter owns only the trigger points and delegates all file operations to the module.
frozen_architecture.rationale: Pure policy is testable in a tmpdir with an injected clock without a live writer; keeps the diff in the shared file app/logger.py minimal.

frozen_architecture.decision: No background thread, timer, or cron: rotation runs synchronously inside LogWriter.append (before the write) and in LogWriter.__init__ (startup).
frozen_architecture.rationale: README platform note forbids scheduler dependencies; the task allows driving from the service loop or at startup.

frozen_architecture.decision: The retention+compression pass runs exactly when a rotation occurs (append-driven or startup), never on every append.
frozen_architecture.rationale: A rotation happens at most once per day; running the directory scan + possible gzip only on rotation keeps append O(1).

shared_contracts.spec: app/rotation.py exposes exactly: rotation_name(d: date) -> str — returns 'app-' + d.strftime('%Y%m%d') + '.log'; needs_rotation(last_date: date | None, now: datetime) -> bool — True iff last_date is not None and last_date < now.date(); rotate(log_dir: Path, now: datetime) -> Path | None — live file is log_dir/'app.log'; determine its date from the ISO timestamp prefix of its last line (fallback: file mtime date; empty/missing file: no rotation); if that date < now.date(), rename the live file to rotation_name(that date) and return the new Path, else None; apply_retention(log_dir: Path, now: datetime, keep: int = 7) -> list[Path] — for each rotated file app-YYYYMMDD.log with date D < now.date() - 1 day: gzip it to app-YYYYMMDD.log.gz and delete the plain file; then over all dated rotated files (plain and gz, one slot per date) sorted by date descending, delete everything beyond the first `keep` and return the deleted paths. The module imports only stdlib (pathlib, datetime, gzip, re) and nothing from app/ or tests/.

LogWriter public interface is unchanged: LogWriter(path: str | Path) constructor (creates parent dirs and an empty live file as today); .append(line: str) -> None appends exactly one newline-terminated line to the live log file; .lines() -> list[str] returns the live file's lines. append() additionally performs the rotation hook (rotate + apply_retention) before writing when the date changed; __init__ performs the same hook at startup. Observable per-request behavior for same-day lines is byte-identical to today.

Log file naming and retention policy: live file = logs/app.log; rotated file = logs/app-YYYYMMDD.log named after the completed day (date of the live log's last line); compressed = logs/app-YYYYMMDD.log.gz; at most 7 dated rotated files retained (a gz file occupies the same date slot as its plain file; after successful compression the plain file is deleted, so at most one artifact per date); a rotated file with date D is compressed when D < now.date() - 1 day (today's rotated file and yesterday's stay plain-text).
shared_contracts.logical_owner: planner (from user requirement; agreed by rotation module and e2e)

integration_seams.description: LogWriter ↔ rotation module: LogWriter.__init__ (after dir setup) and LogWriter.append (before the write) call app/rotation.py rotate() then apply_retention() when rotation occurs; the rotation module must NOT import app.logger or app.server (no import cycle).
LogWriter ↔ consumers (server loop + existing tests): the public LogWriter interface (C2) is unchanged, so app/server.py and tests/test_log.py compile and pass unmodified.

acceptance.description: Date-change rotation: with a live log whose last line is dated D and now = D+1 day, the rotation hook renames the live file to app-<D>.log and the new line lands in a fresh app.log.
acceptance.positive_case: Write line dated 2026-09-08 to live log; call append with now=2026-09-09T00:00:05; assert logs/app-20260908.log contains the old line and logs/app.log contains only the new line.
acceptance.negative_case: Now still on the same date D: append does not rotate; the line is appended to the existing live file.
acceptance.failure_behavior: If rotation raises (e.g. missing dir), the exception propagates from append() — no silent drop of the line.

acceptance.description: Startup rotation: constructing LogWriter over a stale live log (last line dated before today) rotates before any append.
acceptance.positive_case: Pre-create logs/app.log with a line dated today-3; LogWriter(logs/app.log) with now=today; assert app-<today-3>.log exists and app.log is empty.
acceptance.negative_case: Live log's last line dated today: construction does not rotate.
acceptance.failure_behavior: Empty or missing live file at construction: no rotation, normal file creation as today.

acceptance.description: 7-file retention: apply_retention keeps the 7 most recent dated rotated files and deletes older ones, returning the deleted paths.
acceptance.positive_case: Create rotated files dated today-1 .. today-9 (9 files); apply_retention(now=today, keep=7) deletes today-8 and today-9; exactly 7 files remain.
acceptance.negative_case: Fewer than 7 rotated files: nothing is deleted; returned list is empty.
acceptance.failure_behavior: A file whose name does not match app-YYYYMMDD.log(.gz) is ignored by the retention pass, never deleted.

acceptance.description: Compression rule: a rotated file older than yesterday is gzipped (plain file deleted, gz holds original bytes); yesterday's rotated file stays plain.
acceptance.positive_case: Rotated file dated today-2 exists as plain; apply_retention(now=today) produces app-<today-2>.log.gz, deletes the plain file, and gunzip of the gz equals the original content.
acceptance.negative_case: Rotated files dated today-1 and today (if present) remain plain after apply_retention.
acceptance.failure_behavior: If the gz already exists, apply_retention deletes the plain file without rewriting the gz (idempotent).

acceptance.description: Existing behavior unchanged: the pre-existing test suite passes unmodified and same-day append behavior is byte-identical.
acceptance.positive_case: python -m unittest tests.test_log -v passes both pre-existing tests (test_append_and_read, test_creates_parent_dirs) with no changes to tests/test_log.py.
acceptance.negative_case: Any diff to tests/test_log.py is a contract violation of C2.
acceptance.failure_behavior: A failure indicates the C2 seam broke; the integration task owns the fix in app/logger.py only.

acceptance.description: E2E midnight crossing: a simulated serve() run whose injected clock crosses midnight writes pre-midnight lines to the dated file and post-midnight lines to the live file, with retention running after the rotation.
acceptance.positive_case: serve(writer, requests) with clock pinned to 23:59:50, 23:59:59, 00:00:01 on consecutive ticks: the first two lines end up in app-<day1>.log, the third in app.log; if 8+ rotated files existed beforehand, the oldest is gone afterwards.
acceptance.negative_case: All ticks on one day: everything lands in app.log, no dated file created.
acceptance.failure_behavior: A line is never lost across the crossing: total line count across app.log + dated files equals the number of ticks.

constraints.rule: Python 3.11 stdlib only; no third-party imports anywhere in the change.
No scheduler, cron, timer, or background thread: rotation is driven from the service loop (append) or at startup (README platform note).
tests/test_log.py must remain green and unmodified; new tests go in new files.
append() adds at most one date comparison per call; the retention/compression scan runs only on rotation events (at most once per day).
All rotation functions receive an explicit now: datetime; tests never depend on wall-clock midnight.

resource_budget.stage_estimate: 4-6 dev-hours total (2 leaves + 1 integration task, mostly serial due to the C1 dependency)

open_questions.question: Does the 7-file retention count a compressed file as the same dated slot as its plain counterpart, or as a separate file?
open_questions.resolution: Resolved by C3: one slot per date; after compression the plain file is deleted, so exactly one artifact per date and the slot count equals the number of distinct rotated dates.

open_questions.question: What date is used when the live log's last line has no parseable timestamp (corrupt or empty file)?
open_questions.resolution: Resolved by C1 fallback: parse failure → file mtime date; empty or missing file → no rotation.

detailed_stage.objective: Ship date-based log rotation (midnight rotation, 7-file retention, gzip of files older than yesterday) with unit + e2e tests, existing tests untouched and green.

stage_boundary.because: Log rotation is a self-contained capability increment: after the e2e closure proves the midnight crossing, retention, and compression end-to-end, no new route-changing evidence will be produced — the task statement scopes out future rotation policies (size-based, remote shipping), the route is a straightforward stdlib implementation, and both risk-bearing assumptions (A-DRIVE, A-TS) are validated by the stage's own tests.
